evidence_excerpts: A program’s WCET is computed by finding the maximum path WCET for all feasible paths; the path leading to the WCET is called the worst-case execution path. The source example reduces one WCEP block by 40 cycles but lowers global WCET only from 205 to 195 cycles.
text: Static WCET reduction depends on optimizing the worst-case execution path, because reducing a noncritical path or a local block can leave the global WCET unchanged or only partly reduced.
